# Solving Names Do Not End the Quest

Metaphysics has usually followed a very primitive kind of quest.[^1] The universe has always appeared to the natural mind as a kind of enigma, of which the key must be sought in the shape of some illuminating or power-bringing word or name.[^2] That word names the universe's PRINCIPLE, and to possess it is, after a fashion, to possess the universe itself.[^3] 'God,' 'Matter,' 'Reason,' 'the Absolute,' 'Energy,' are so many solving names.[^4] You can rest when you have them.[^5] You are at the end of your metaphysical quest.[^6]

But if you follow the pragmatic method, you cannot look on any such word as closing your quest.[^7] You must bring out of each word its practical cash-value, set it at work within the stream of your experience.[^8] It appears less as a solution, then, than as a program for more work, and more particularly as an indication of the ways in which existing realities may be CHANGED.[^9]
